key_insight: Nitrogen vacancies locally weaken polar-axis lattice coupling in wurtzite AlN, enabling nucleation and redirecting ferroelectric domain growth according to vacancy distribution and switching sequence.
engineering_relevance: Engineering nitrogen vacancies, whose formation is promoted by scandium doping, could lower coercive fields and support low-voltage AlN-based ferroelectric memory.
method: Density functional theory for atomic-scale mechanisms
Deep Potential molecular dynamics for domain-growth kinetics
Experimental characterization to connect simulations with observed behavior
evidence_signal: The combined calculations, simulations and experiments link vacancy-mediated switching to domain-growth patterns that differ from ideal-crystal predictions, although the abstract reports no numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: Device implementation requires control of vacancy distribution; the abstract does not establish an optimal defect concentration or quantify reliability trade-offs.
paper_title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
